page: Amazon Web Services c6id.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.

A key feature of this instance is its bundled local storage, consisting of a 474 GB NVMe SSD. This local storage provides high-speed, low-latency data access directly attached to the hypervisor. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The instance does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the instance consistently in the average tier for its hardware class. The single-core Geekbench score is 1610.0, while the multi-core score is 6004.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 413.67 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 58.2 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For database operations, the instance achieves 7.96 million Redis SET operations per second and a Passmark database score of 3953.04. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and medium-sized LLM inference tasks show weaker relative performance, with 7B model text generation reaching 8.21 tokens per second.

The c6id.2xlarge offers a balanced cost-to-performance profile for compute-intensive workloads requiring fast local scratch space. The inclusion of dedicated vCPUs and high-speed NVMe storage makes it highly suitable for applications such as medium-scale databases, static web serving, data compression tasks, and distributed build systems.
